Benchmark.title: AEGIS Web Server Security Benchmark
Benchmark.description: Security configuration assessment for web servers based on CIS and NIST 800-53 controls. Evaluates TLS configuration, security headers, access controls, and common misconfigurations.

Rule.title: Enforce TLS 1.2 or Higher
Rule.description: The server must only support TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3. SSLv3 and TLS 1.0/1.1 are deprecated and vulnerable to POODLE, BEAST, and downgrade attacks (NIST SP 800-52r2).
Rule.fixtext: Disable SSLv3, TLS 1.0, and TLS 1.1 in the server configuration. For nginx: ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; For Apache: SSLProtocol -all +TLSv1.2 +TLSv1.3

Rule.title: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) Header Required
Rule.description: The Strict-Transport-Security header must be present with a minimum max-age of 31536000 (1 year). Without HSTS, users are vulnerable to SSL stripping and downgrade attacks.
Rule.fixtext: Add header: Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload

Rule.title: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Required
Rule.description: A Content-Security-Policy header must be configured to prevent XSS, clickjacking, and code injection attacks. CSP restricts the sources from which content can be loaded.
Rule.fixtext: Add header: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'

Rule.title: X-Frame-Options Header Required
Rule.description: X-Frame-Options must be set to DENY or SAMEORIGIN to prevent clickjacking attacks where the page is embedded in a malicious iframe.
Rule.fixtext: Add header: X-Frame-Options: DENY (or SAMEORIGIN if framing from same origin is required)

Rule.title: X-Content-Type-Options Header Required
Rule.description: The X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header prevents MIME-type sniffing, which can lead to XSS attacks via content-type confusion.

Rule.title: Server Version Disclosure Must Be Suppressed
Rule.description: The Server HTTP response header must not reveal software name or version information. Version disclosure enables targeted attacks against known vulnerabilities in specific versions.
Rule.fixtext: For nginx: server_tokens off; For Apache: ServerTokens Prod and ServerSignature Off

Rule.title: Directory Listing Must Be Disabled
Rule.description: Web server directory listing (autoindex) must be disabled. Exposed directory listings reveal internal file structure, backup files, configuration files, and other sensitive data to attackers.
Rule.fixtext: For nginx: autoindex off; For Apache: Options -Indexes in httpd.conf or .htaccess

Rule.title: Session Cookies Must Have Secure and HttpOnly Flags
Rule.description: All session cookies must include the Secure flag (HTTPS-only transmission) and HttpOnly flag (prevents JavaScript access). Missing flags allow session hijacking via XSS or network sniffing.
Rule.fixtext: Set cookie flags: Set-Cookie: session=value; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict

Rule.title: CORS Policy Must Not Use Wildcard Origin
Rule.description: Access-Control-Allow-Origin must not be set to '*' in production. Wildcard CORS allows any website to make authenticated requests to the application, potentially leading to data theft.
Rule.fixtext: Replace Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * with specific trusted domains. Use Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: false if wildcard is necessary.

Rule.title: Default Administrative Credentials Must Be Changed
Rule.description: All default usernames and passwords for web applications, databases, and management interfaces must be changed before deployment. Default credentials are publicly documented and trivially exploitable.
Rule.fixtext: Change all default passwords. Implement strong password policy (minimum 12 characters, complexity requirements). Enable MFA for administrative access.

Rule.title: Verbose Error Messages Must Be Disabled in Production
Rule.description: Stack traces, debug output, and detailed error messages must not be displayed to end users. Verbose errors reveal internal paths, database schemas, and technology stack information useful for exploitation.
Rule.fixtext: Set display_errors=Off in PHP. Use custom error pages. Configure production logging to file with generic user-facing error messages.

Rule.title: Administrative Interfaces Must Not Use Default Paths
Rule.description: Administrative panels accessible at predictable paths (/admin, /wp-admin, /phpmyadmin, /console) are primary targets for brute-force and credential stuffing attacks.
Rule.fixtext: Rename admin paths to non-default URLs. Restrict admin access by IP whitelist. Implement rate limiting and account lockout on login endpoints.

rule-result.message: TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 are enabled on port 443. Only TLS 1.2+ should be permitted.
Strict-Transport-Security header is missing from HTTPS responses.
No Content-Security-Policy header detected. XSS protections are incomplete.
X-Frame-Options header is absent. Page is vulnerable to clickjacking.
Server header reveals: nginx/1.22.1. Software version is disclosed.
Directory listing is enabled on /images/ and /docs/ paths exposing file structure.
Session cookie 'PHPSESSID' is missing Secure and HttpOnly flags.
Default credentials admin/password detected on login page.
PHP display_errors=On. Full stack traces visible in error responses, revealing /var/www/html/dvwa/ path.
